newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to keep money supply loose on stable CPI.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to keep money supply loose on stable CPI.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank pledged on Saturday to maintain an "appropriately loose" monetary policy, noting that consumer price growth was well within government targets.

"Growth of the consumer price index in the first nine months of 1996 averaged 3.05 percent, falling within the government target of 3.6 percent, so the central bank will maintain an appropriately loose monetary policy in the near term," central bank research director Chien Chi-min told reporters.
Taiwan's September consumer price index rose 3.84 percent compared to a year earlier, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Saturday.
On a month-to-month basis, the September consumer price index was down 0.55 percent from August, the directorate said.
At the wholesale level, September wholesale prices were down 3.29 percent from September 1995 and down 0.30 percent from August 1996.
The easing rate of consumer price increases reflected the market's recovery from a spate of typhoons in July and August that damaged crops and sent vegetable and fruit prices soaring.
Despite dramatic storm-related upticks in food prices in August, consumer prices in the first nine months of 1996 rose at an average of 3.05 percent per month.
In August, the directorate forecast that consumer prices were on track to climb 3.33 percent for all of calendar 1996.
